column1: # A baseline for tables/state_media_items.tsv: items of central state and Party media on Nvidia chips, Jan 1, 2024 to Jun 30, 2025, in that table's columns and by its rule: 174 rows (171 held: saved and read whole; 3 found: known and not saved). The first 49 were made on Nov 25, 2026, row by row as each page was read; 125 were added on Nov 26, 2026 (the line before the columns says how). NOT A CENSUS, and gathered by other routes than that table: web searches; the saved pages of state outlets dated in those months; every item of those months in the index of the Yuyuan Tantian account on CCTV's site; and a scan of the titles of the daily editions of four papers (People's Daily, its Overseas Edition, Economic Daily, Guangming Daily), whose articles naming Nvidia were saved and read. The rows are kept apart: none is counted in tables/state_media_items.tsv. Scope, as that table's: one row per item of a central state or Party outlet (an item carried by several pages is one row, with the other carriers in column 10); commercial and local outlets only as carriers; items that do not name Nvidia or its chips are left out, and so are items that name Nvidia only in a passage on the world market (share prices, global demand, a new product, another country's deals) with nothing on Chinese buyers, the Chinese market, American curbs on China or Chinese alternatives. The items left out are in tables/state_media_baseline_outside_scope.tsv, each with its reason. Stance rule (that table's): warns = the item, in its own words or a speaker's it quotes, says Nvidia's chips carry security risks, or that Nvidia must prove them safe, or argues against buying or using them; mixed = that, together with words that Nvidia or American chipmakers are welcome or that imports may resume; a sentence that only reports or predicts buyers' reluctance is not a warning; welcomes (favours imports or Nvidia's presence); neutral (reports without advice); self-reliance (stresses home-made chips without advice on buying); other. Each stance was decided from the saved page read whole: 1 warns, 0 mixed, 15 welcome, 79 neutral, 57 self-reliance, 22 other. A second reading of 28 of the first 46 held pages differed on three rows, none of them on a warning; each row added on Nov 26, 2026 was coded five times. Two flags stand at the start of the note (column 12): REPORTS-AUTHORITY = the item only reports an authority's act or words without comment, classed by the rule as written (8 rows); GROUP-PAPER = a paper of the People's Daily group that tables/state_media_items.tsv never holds (Securities Times, People's Tribune, China City News: 14 rows), so a comparison with that table counts the other 160.

# Added Nov 26, 2026. (a) The last 125 rows: every saved page of an outlet in scope dated January 2024 to June 2025 that names Nvidia or its chips and was not yet a row or a row's carrier, coded by this table's rule five times independently (two readers of every page and three further codings), a majority deciding each cell; pages that carry the same item joined into one row. They were found by a scan of the saved pages, not by a search list (column 11: -), and stand after the first 49 rows, in the order of their dates. The table is still not a census. Later the same day 3 more of these rows proved to be the same piece as another row on a second site (two independent readers read each pair of pages, with pairs known to be the same and known to differ among them): their pages are named in column 10 of their item's row and the rows are gone, so 125 is the number left. (b) Column 13, subject, for every row: two readings of each page, a third where they differed. Items on a product with an Nvidia chip stay in the table; a count of items about the chips for AI computing takes the rows of that subject. (c) Saved pages found on Nov 26, 2026 to carry an item the table already held are named in column 10 of that item's row.

# Columns: 1 date = the page's own publication date (Beijing time) | 2 outlet = who published the words | 3 kind = signed commentary | unsigned commentary | news | interview | social post | official text carried | analysis | notice | 4 stance toward buying Nvidia chips = warns | welcomes | mixed | neutral | self-reliance | other | 5 speaker = whose words the key sentence is | 6 key sentence = exact words from the saved page, checked against the saved copy by script (for the three rows marked found, the words are as the search reported them and are not checked) | 7 saved id of the page that carries the key sentence | 8 held = saved and read whole | found = known, not saved | 9 original? = original outlet page | outlet's own channel on a platform | relay (another site) | 10 other carriers (saved ids) | 11 the row's place in the search list it came from (- where it was found another way) | 12 note | 13 subject = chips for AI computing | a product with an Nvidia chip | Nvidia as a company | other (an item on another matter that names Nvidia or its chips in passing)
